page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the t2d server family. It is equipped with 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. This configuration features a dedicated CPU allocation with 1.0 thread per core, meaning hyper-threading is not active. The system is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 2692.58, and Geekbench single-core performance is average at 1502.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 5335.58 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2729.0, both landing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 35.65 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 22.54 GB/sec, resulting in a poor PassMark memory score in the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile, the t2d-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring dedicated, non-shared CPU resources without the overhead of hyper-threading. The instance is suitable for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, and simple text processing. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded decompression, or parallel computing tasks due to its constrained memory bandwidth and weak multi-core scaling.

With a dedicated CPU allocation of 1.0 thread per core, it avoids hyper-threading overhead. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng, while multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain in the bottom 25%. It provides a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:4, making it suitable for general-purpose utility tasks.
